Coco Tam's is the beach bar on the sand in Fisherman's Village, Bophut, open daily from about 12:00 to midnight. Its fire shows are free to watch and run twice a night, at about 19:15 and 21:00, in front of more than 200 beanbags. There is no entry fee and beanbags are first come, first served, so arrive by about 17:30 for a seat; cocktails cost about 250–400 THB, and booked front tables can carry a minimum spend.

Map and location

Coco Tam's sits directly on Bophut beach, between the beach road and the sea, close to The Wharf at the western end of the village. From the beach road you walk through a small garden to the bar; the beanbags are laid out on the sand in front, facing north towards Koh Phangan. The map shows Coco Tam's, The Wharf car park and the rest of Fisherman's Village.

Fire show times and weekly schedule

  1. 12:00 Opens for drinks and food; quiet in the afternoon.
  2. 17:00 Beach road fills up; on Fridays the Walking Street starts.
  3. 17:30 Best time to claim a beanbag for sunset and the first show.
  4. 19:15 First fire show on the sand.
  5. 21:00 Second fire show.
  6. 24:00 Close.

Some 2026 listings give the second show at 21:30 and a few older reviews put the first at 19:30, so if you are coming specially for the later show, check on the day. Shows are cancelled or cut short in heavy rain, which is most likely from October to December.

What it is like

Coco Tam's is a large, open-air bamboo-and-thatch beach bar rather than a club. The draw is the setting: low beanbags and platform beds on the sand, swing seats at the bar, hanging chairs, cabanas, warm lighting under the palms and the lights of Koh Phangan across the water. The bar says it can serve up to 400 people at once, and on a Friday in high season it does.

The fire shows are the reason most people come. A troupe of performers spins, flips and breathes fire to loud music, a few metres from the front row; it is a proper show, and children love it. Between shows the mood is relaxed: people lying back on beanbags with a cocktail, and a few vendors walking the sand with light-up toys. On Fridays and Saturdays a DJ turns the volume up, and some guests in 2026 complained that the music drowned out the performers.

Two practical points from repeated guest feedback: the front row smells of the kerosene used for the fire, so a row or two back is more comfortable, and service slows down badly at peak times. Order your next drink before the show starts.

Food, drinks and prices

The menu is Italian-leaning beach food: wood-fired pizza (the most praised dish), pasta, burgers, seafood, salads, a few Thai dishes such as pad thai, and mango sticky rice. The cocktail list runs to more than two dozen drinks served in jar glasses, and the house favourite is the Dark Passion (vodka, passion fruit and watermelon). Shisha is offered; reviewers rate it poor value.

ItemTypical price (THB)
CocktailAbout 250–400
Cocktail at a pop-up bar on the Friday market, for comparisonAbout 70–99
Street-food dinner on the Friday market, for comparisonAbout 300–500 per person

Coco Tam's does not publish its menu prices online, so we quote only the cocktail range we could verify; beer, pizza and burgers are priced like a beach bar, well above the market stalls, and fries are ordered separately with burgers. The beach area has taken cash only; the bar and restaurant take cards, with a 3 % surcharge reported.

Minimum spends and seating

  • Beanbags: first come, first served, with no charge beyond what you order. Management says walk-ins are free before 18:00 and around both shows.
  • Front and "VIP" tables: some carry a minimum spend that depends on the view and whether you eat. In 2026 guests reported a 1,000 THB per person tab for a front section and 2,500 THB per person for a booked evening table, paid up front. Ask before you sit.
  • Bookings: walk-ins are fine for drinks and the show; book ahead for a dining table on Fridays and weekends. Some guests were told weekend reservations weren't taken, so confirm the day before.

Its daytime sister venue on the same beach, Summer by Coco Tam's, has a 500 THB per person minimum spend. [check] There is also a small speakeasy-style bar upstairs, Easy on Tam's, for a quieter drink after the show. [check]

Tips

Best time to go

  • For a good seat: arrive by 17:30, order food and stay through dusk for the 19:15 show.
  • For a quieter night: Monday to Thursday, when you can usually find a beanbag for the 21:00 show without arriving early.
  • Friday: walk the Walking Street from 17:00, eat at the stalls and come down for the 21:00 show, when the market crowd has thinned.

What to bring

  • Cash in baht for the beach area and small notes for the vendors selling light-up toys.
  • A card for the bar if you plan to eat, and a little patience at peak times: order your next round before the show.

Safety

  • Keep children seated and well back from the performers; sparks and fuel fumes carry.
  • Bophut beach is one of Thailand's no-smoking beaches, with fines of up to 100,000 THB.
  • Don't swim here at night, or after drinking. We don't recommend swimming at Bophut at all; see Bophut Beach.

Getting there and home

From Chaweng, Grab costs about 150–250 THB and takes 15–20 minutes; ask to be dropped at The Wharf. On Fridays the beach road closes to traffic from about 16:30, The Wharf car park fills after about 18:00, and badly parked scooters are towed (500 THB or more to release), so a Grab or taxi is the easy option. Songthaews mostly stop by 20:00–22:00, so book your ride home before the second show ends. More in getting around Koh Samui.

Who it suits, and who should go elsewhere

Go if you want a relaxed evening with a free fire show: couples, families with children (come for the 19:15 show), friends after dinner in the village, and anyone doing the Friday market.

Go elsewhere if you want a real party: the late-night action is in Chaweng at ARKbar and on Soi Green Mango, 15–20 minutes away. If you want a quiet, unhurried dinner, book one of the village restaurants instead and walk down for the 21:00 show afterwards. Compare all the options in our beach clubs guide and Koh Samui nightlife.

Events and holidays

  • Loy Krathong, Tuesday 24 November 2026: krathongs are floated from Bophut beach; it is also a Full Moon Party night on Koh Phangan.
  • New Year's Eve, Thursday 31 December 2026: Fisherman's Village has the second-biggest fireworks on Samui after Chaweng, and the beach is packed from early evening. Book a table well ahead and come by taxi.
